cells.tense: The practice is running now, and nothing in it is being forced.
cells.ask: End one session at a plain stopping point while there's still something left in you, then let the rest of the day have you.
cells.core:
Practice fits you right now. You put in the time and it comes back as something you can do with your hands, and the quiet around it is yours, not a wall. That steadiness is easy to overlook while it's working.

You can also feel the whole shape of the work while you're inside it — where it's carrying you, and where the next thing worth learning sits. That's the vantage most people lose while they practice. You don't have to hunt for the next opening. Just protect this: end one sitting before it ends you, and let what you have made stay made. Letting the day have you is part of it.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is yours and it's working. Keep it that way.
cells.verb: keeping one small thing lit by showing up to it again
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole shape while still inside it

cells.tense: The next standard is already ahead of you, and you are running toward it.
cells.ask: Close one session at the point it was set to end, imperfect, and leave the room without correcting anything.
cells.core:
This has turned into guarding. The next thing to refine is waiting ahead of you, and a flaw in the work gets answered by another pass, then another, and by the time you look up the hour is gone. The quiet around it has stopped being chosen.

Stopping is the move you keep not spending. The standard you're holding is real, and it can hold for one evening without your hands on it. Close one session at the point it was set to end, imperfect, and leave the room without correcting anything. What you did not fix will still be there tomorrow, and it will be smaller than it looks now.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding the work, not doing it.

cells.tense: There is a place you keep almost going, and it stays unconsumed.
cells.ask: Take one small step you have done before, tell one person you're doing it, and add nothing else for now.
cells.core:
There's a place you keep almost going. A class, a morning ritual, the instrument in the corner — you get near the starting line and the reason to skip arrives, then you're somewhere else. What you can do, you do under pressure, or when nobody's watching.

The wall isn't laziness. It's that practice stopped being a place you return to. You don't need to walk through it today. Take one small step you have done before, tell one person you're doing it, and add nothing else for now. Not the whole practice. Just the part where the two-way street starts moving again.
cells.sheetLine: You can do it under pressure. You just don't come back to it.

cells.tense: The hand is already steady here, and the making of it goes unnamed.
cells.ask: Say once, plainly, that a skill you already have is something you built, and notice what happens next.
cells.core:
People tell you that you make it look easy, that it just seems to come out of you. The truth is quieter: the same thing done enough times stops asking permission and happens. Good — and it isn't only that. The running also happens whether or not you chose it, so it keeps going past the point where stopping was the answer.

Say once, plainly, that a skill you already have is something you built. You don't have to assemble the years, just admit that repetition did the work. That's what keeps this a practice instead of a machine that runs you.
cells.sheetLine: It doesn't come out of nowhere. It comes from you.
